verdict.line: You lose if you let him land two Q stacks and pull you into a trade before level 2; you win every all-in after level 6 once Counter Strike covers his Path Maker.

brief.thesis: K'Sante's Q (Ntofo Strikes) builds a stack counter on-screen that you must respect: the first hit is just a slow, but the second hit within its 3.5s cooldown fires a shockwave that pulls you in, so he controls when extended trades start. Jax has no answer to that pull before 6, but E (Counter Strike) dodges every basic attack he throws out during the stun window it creates, which flips any trade where he tries to auto-reset through your stun.

theirWindow.what: He is one Q away from the pull shockwave. Do not stand in his 450-range line for a free poke, and don't let him land Q, walk away, then Q again to drag you in.

yourWindow.when: his W (Path Maker) and E (Footwork) are both down
yourWindow.what: Leap in with Q (Leap Strike), pop W (Empower) on the strike, and go for the extended trade — he has no shield and no dash to disengage, and your E stun locks out his autos entirely.

start.why: 52.3% win rate over 1,110 games; the extra AD and sustain matter more than Doran's Shield once you're trading into his Q pokes rather than tanking through them.

boots.why: 53.8% win rate, 57.5% pick rate — his autos and Q strikes are physical, and the reduced auto damage directly undercuts his poke-and-pull pattern.

core.why: 57.9% win rate over 152 games as the first core item; the proc damage and movement speed let you punish the moment his Q is on cooldown.
Pairs with Trinity in the highest win-rate path; the crit/heal proc rewards landing your empowered strikes in extended trades.
Completes the 57.9% path and gives you a way to survive his All Out burst window if he catches you alone.

situational.when: you are ahead and want to no-sell his All Out burst instead of playing around Zhonya's
he is building tank and you need sustained DPS and a slow to chase him down
the lane goes long and you want sustained damage through his All Out tankiness

runes.keystoneWhy: 53.8% win rate, 19.9% pick; the sustain from Grasp procs offsets his Q poke damage over a long lane you can't just burst down early. Master-tier Jax players instead run Lethal Tempo (Precision, 20,493 games) if you're confident playing for extended attack-speed trades rather than passive wave trading — better suited to a player comfortable all-inning early rather than scaling.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is the highest win rate at 52.8% over a 46.3% pick rate; Ignite punishes his Footwork disengage shield and closes out skirmishes he tries to shield-and-reset out of.

playing.title: Track his Q stack count all lane
playing.detail: One stack means the next hit pulls you in — back off instead of trading face-to-face. Zero stacks means you can walk up for a free poke without risking the shockwave.

playing.title: Save E for his engage, not your own
playing.detail: Counter Strike dodges all incoming basic attacks and stuns on a 18/16/14/12/10s cooldown — hold it until he commits to an all-in so you dodge his autos and lock him down, rather than burning it preemptively.

playing.title: All-in the moment W and E are both down
playing.detail: With Path Maker and Footwork on cooldown he has no shield and no disengage. Leap Strike in, Empower the hit, and commit to the extended trade.

playing.title: Respect his All Out past level 6
playing.detail: R knocks you back through terrain and transforms his kit for increased damage and healing. Don't get caught alone near a wall once he has it up — his damage spikes hard during that window.

playing.title: Use R's attack speed to win trades, not start them
playing.detail: Relentless Assault has 0s cooldown and scales off consecutive attacks, so pop it once you're already in the trade from Leap Strike, not as an opener.

playing.title: Reset waves instead of standing in Q range
playing.detail: His Q has a 3.5s cooldown and only a 450 range — crashing the wave and backing off between resets denies him free stacks toward the pull.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and win-rate figures are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the lane-by-lane tactical reading (stack tracking, cooldown windows, trade timing) is my own analysis of the ability kits.
